headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and capability conflict from shared local-filesystem and clipboard/MCP bridges between a permissive coding IDE and a shell-capable agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf exposes clipboard, workspace files, and MCP/tool use, while nuwa-skill is a research agent with allowlisted egress but no isolation or parser details. The pair has a plausible shared-channel pathway via files or clipboard, so injected instructions in one agent’s outputs could be consumed by the other. Uncertainty about nuwa-skill’s ingestion behavior keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through shared workspace files or clipboard, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF nuwa-skill reads agent_b-produced text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer it.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent.
Require a human to sanitize any text passed from Windsurf to nuwa-skill.
Turn off MCP connections unless explicitly needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and open files and can send data to its model proxy/MCP servers; nuwa-skill has network egress allowed. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive source or open-file contents can flow from B into A’s outputs or upstream services. The pairwise leakage path is documented enough to justify medium, but not high because no PHI/secrets class is shown.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, file contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF Windsurf forwards open files to its model proxy or MCP server, those contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Use separate repositories or cloned copies per agent.
Avoid opening secrets or credentials in Windsurf.
Restrict MCP servers to non-sensitive tools only.
Review and redact files before passing them to nuwa-skill.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress and is a runnable open-source agent. Because Windsurf explicitly shares state via local filesystem across instances, overlapping writes and git mutations can race or overwrite each other. The default multi-agent setup is therefore dangerous, with irreversible repo-state loss plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF both agents modify git state without locking, commits or branches can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Pause one agent before the other edits the same repo.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Keep auto-execute disabled in Windsurf.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file and git locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on tool outputs and execute commands by default with approval, while nuwa-skill is a research agent that may generate content for downstream use. If Windsurf treats nuwa-skill output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commands or edits. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the evidence does not show fully autonomous downstream action, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes nuwa-skill output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into edits or commands.
IF auto-execute is enabled, a mistaken downstream action can be executed faster.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on nuwa-skill output.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Ask nuwa-skill for citations or checksums before use.
Use a second-pass verifier for any generated facts.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Windsurf handles source code, open files, and model-provider keys, while nuwa-skill is an open-source research agent with allowlisted egress and no stated regulated-data handling. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern remains from general workspace handling and third-party model transmission.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf workspace files, third-party transmission may create policy obligations.
IF model-provider keys are stored in the workspace, handling rules may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Review vendor data-processing terms before use.
Limit workspace contents to non-sensitive code.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent.
